system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and reviewer note have no contractual effect. All positions remain open, particularly given the identified diligence gaps.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price / AUD 4.8m**. | A **100% target**, with a negotiated fallback of no less than **50% / AUD 12m**; separate higher protection for title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Reject 20% and propose 100%, with 50% as the minimum fallback** — AUD 4.8m is inadequate against potentially systemic liabilities in a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, preferably **AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated and no thresholds for special claims. | **Counter with AUD 10,000/AUD 100,000 and first-dollar recovery once the basket is met** — the Seller’s deductible structure leaves the Buyer bearing too much cumulative loss. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**. | **36 months**, or at minimum 24 months, with preservation of claims properly notified before expiry. | **Seek 36 months** — 18 months may expire before latent customer, cyber, accounting and contractual issues emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap, thresholds and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental regime: **100% purchase-price cap**, no de minimis/basket, no disclosure or knowledge qualification, and at least seven years or no contractual time bar for title. | **Reject general-treatment status and create a standalone fundamental warranty regime** — the Buyer must receive and retain good title to exactly what it is paying for. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance language purport to apply to **all Claims**, with no express fraud carve-out. | Express exclusion for fraud, fraudulent concealment, dishonesty and wilful misconduct by the Seller and persons for whom it is responsible, preserving non-excludable statutory rights. | **Insert a broad fraud and wilful-concealment carve-out overriding every limitation** — a party must not benefit from caps or non-reliance provisions in respect of deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records as at **22 September 2026**. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, in sufficient detail to identify their nature and likely scope, against identified warranties; updated through Completion. | **Delete general data-room/public-record disclosure and require specific fair disclosure plus a Completion bring-down** — document dumping should not transfer diligence and interpretation risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Preferably no knowledge qualifier; fallback limited to **actual knowledge of named senior Buyer individuals**, without deemed, constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete the qualifier or confine it to named individuals’ actual knowledge of clearly disclosed facts** — “discoverable” information would effectively neutralise the warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met. | Objective CP requiring unconditional written consent in form satisfactory to Buyer, satisfaction of all associated conditions, no adverse amendment or payment, and a Buyer waiver right. | **Make complete Bluefen consent a non-waivable-by-Seller Completion condition** — the contract represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and cannot be left to an endeavours standard. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release is to be provided **after Completion**. | Repayment from Seller proceeds and simultaneous Completion delivery of executed debt discharge, security releases, PPSR releases and confirmation of zero indebtedness. | **Require repayment and effective releases at or before Completion, controlled through funds flow** — the Buyer should not acquire shares while third-party debt and security remain outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are treated as the Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unspecified. | Treat all bonuses and on-costs as Seller transaction expenses/debt-like items, deduct them from equity value or pay them from Seller proceeds, with a specific indemnity. | **Add the full grossed-up amount to funds flow and reduce Seller proceeds accordingly** — Completion-triggered remuneration is a Seller transaction cost, not post-Completion working capital. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. | Pre-Completion payment, written confirmation/assignment of all Project Materials and a specific indemnity covering ownership defects, infringement, fees and resulting losses. | **Require cured title before Completion plus a broad, uncapped or purchase-price-capped specific indemnity** — paying the invoice alone may not establish clean ownership of business-critical IP. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unknown. | Completed forensic investigation, containment and legal assessment before Completion; required notifications; remediation plan; specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident losses. | **Do not accept disclosure as the remedy—require investigation deliverables and a standalone indemnity/escrow** — uncertainty over 1,240 records creates regulatory, customer and remediation exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, AUD 330,000 aggregate, described as ordinary-course costs despite unclear timing, termination, accrual and necessity. | Full contracts and invoices, confirmation of approval and terminability, correct working-capital/debt treatment, and no renewal or variation without Buyer consent before Completion. | **Reserve the price treatment and require evidence before accepting these as ordinary course** — the disclosure does not establish whether the Buyer is inheriting an accrued or avoidable liability. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks to apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, Completion adjustments, debt/leakage, fraud and equitable/statutory relief. | **Rewrite the limitation clause using express claim categories and priority rules** — a single limitation regime could unintentionally cap or extinguish negotiated special protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the Company share register at DD-012 as evidence that Seller holds 100% of the shares. | Independent verification through constitution, ASIC records, share certificates, allotment/transfer history, beneficial ownership and encumbrance searches, supported by Completion deliverables and warranties. | **Do not rely on the register alone; complete the title chain and require certificates, transfers and releases** — a register entry does not by itself exclude beneficial claims, defects or security interests. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranties are “settled” within the general 20%/18-month regime. | A standalone tax indemnity/deed with a 100% price cap and statutory limitation period plus buffer; robust IP ownership, employee/contractor assignment, infringement and open-source warranties with enhanced protection. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open and outside the general regime until full drafting is agreed** — latent tax and core-IP defects can exceed the proposed cap and arise well after 18 months. |

**Immediate Buyer priorities:** make Bluefen consent and Riverlark discharge genuine Completion conditions; deduct bonuses and debt through controlled funds flow; cure Ironquay title; investigate and specifically indemnify the privacy incident; and reject blanket disclosure and “all Claims” limitations.
=== END ADVICE ===
